checks.finding: Reviewed all 13 tasks' Risk tier against Scope/Done When/Goal sentinel-surface signals per risk-classification-policy.md. High/critical tasks (T-002 canonicalizer, T-003 HMAC signer, T-004 approver-registry schema, T-005 weakening detector, T-006 validator, T-007 publisher [critical], T-008 handshake, T-009 guard-invariants registration [critical], T-010 hook-guard boundary verification, T-011/T-012 track-selection consumer migration) each cite a specific sensitive surface (secrets handling, access control, irreversible protected-file mutation) matching risk-classification-policy.md:16-17. Medium tasks (T-001 wholly-new schemas with no consumer yet — 'Breaking API: no; all three files are wholly new' — and T-013 closing audit, 'no production logic change') correctly reflect no sentinel-surface exposure at time of task landing. No task's scope is limited to only UI copy/CSS/docs/test-only content while carrying a high/critical tier: T-010 is test-only but its Risk Rationale ties directly to a genuine security stake (a false-positive 96-cell denial-matrix result would leave protected sidecar/registry/sentinel paths effectively unguarded while claiming otherwise), matching policy's 'silent defect causes material harm' high-tier trigger rather than routine test-only busywork.

Every Risk: high/critical task (T-002 through T-012) includes in its Done When section both TDD Red→Green evidence ('Red' failing-suite capture before implementation, 'Green' passing-run capture after) and an independent quality-gate verdict recorded by 'a named second reviewer, not the implementing agent.' The two Risk: critical tasks (T-007, T-009) additionally require 'a second, distinct named approver additionally reviews and signs the evidence bundle,' matching risk-classification-policy.md:17's two-person-approval-plus-signed-evidence requirement.

T-001 ('Author the project-context.yaml and provider-bindings.yaml schemas', tasks.md lines 122-330) has 11 distinct Done-When checklist items (TEST-001, TEST-002, TEST-003, TEST-004, TEST-040, TEST-041, TEST-042, suite self-registration, staged test.yml+MANIFEST evidence, CHANGELOG entry, acceptance-first+independent-review evidence) — exceeding the '>8 distinct verifiable items' oversized-task indicator. Its Scope also bundles at least 4 distinct implementation areas in one task: `contracts/project-context.schema.json`, `contracts/project-context.template.yaml` (single-source cross-cutting seed-list scaffold), `contracts/provider-bindings.schema.json`, and cross-schema `DUPLICATE_COMPONENT_ID`/`DUPLICATE_BINDING_ID`/`adapter_paths` semantic-test coverage — exceeding the '>3 distinct implementation areas' indicator. T-002 is a secondary, more marginal instance (9 Done-When items). Note: T-001's own text cites 'Accepted-deviation record (decision-7 = A): specs/epic-189-a1-project-context/verification/T-001/sizing-accepted-deviation.md,' indicating this exact tension was previously raised and a human recorded a decision on it; that file is outside this review's 14-file allowed-input manifest and was not read. Per this role's 'never waive a finding' mandate, this finding reports the current, directly-observed artifact fact regardless — the accepted-deviation pointer is included here as context for the orchestrator, not as grounds for suppressing the count-based evidence above.

Every functional task's associated AC set includes at least one explicit negative/rejection/boundary/fail-closed acceptance criterion, not happy-path-only: T-001→AC-001/AC-003 (parameterized required-field rejection), AC-040 (duplicate-id rejection); T-002→AC-005 (4-category rejection lock), AC-037 (boundary vectors); T-003→AC-011 (fail-closed no-key path), AC-034 (mid-write-failure recovery); T-004→AC-044 (malformed-registry rejection), AC-045 (duplicate-id rejection), AC-046 (zero-identity boundary); T-005→AC-017 (non-weakening negative proof), AC-030 (anchor-injection-attempt rejection), AC-031 (glob-narrowing boundary cases); T-006→AC-014 (six-way negative proof), AC-043 (underapproval rejection); T-007→AC-033 (symlink denial, multi-target crash-recovery boundary cases); T-008→AC-027 (fail-closed verify-response), AC-032 (cleanup-failure/stale-sentinel cases); T-010→AC-023 (pure protected-write denial matrix); T-011/T-012→AC-026 (PROJECT_CONTEXT_INVALID explicit-stop, distinct from the happy-path compatibility fallback).

acceptance-tests.md does not use literal unit/integration/e2e/acceptance vocabulary (a schema+security-infrastructure epic with no application UI layers to which those labels natively apply); each TEST-NNN row instead carries a specific, descriptive Test Type whose stated scope matches its Test Target. Examples: TEST-001..TEST-004/TEST-040..TEST-042 ('parameterized schema conformance', 'field-allowlist coverage', 'provider-neutrality proof') each target one schema file — unit-equivalent scope, not overstated; TEST-009 ('multi-runtime hash-equality + dispatch proof') genuinely spans 4 runtime components (.py/.sh/.ps1/.js) — integration-equivalent scope, not understated as a narrow unit check; TEST-025/TEST-039 ('behavior lock', 'full per-consumer common-contract-suite matrix') genuinely exercise complete consumer decision workflows across 5 skill files — end-to-end-equivalent scope. Every row is keyed to a specific AC-NNN by the table's own structure. No declared test type was found to understate or overstate its Test Target's actual scope.

Every Risk: high/critical task (T-002 through T-012) carries an explicit `Rollback:` field. Tasks whose output stays staging-only until a later task applies it (e.g. T-002, T-003) correctly note that reverting leaves no live-state change to roll back ('staging-only output'). Tasks whose staged output is human-applied to a protected live path within the same task (T-009, T-012) carry the more precise caveat that reverting the agent-authored commit does NOT automatically revert an already-human-applied change, and that the revert PR must state explicitly whether a human should also hand-revert the application — matching infra-spec.md's Rollback section verbatim.

Global Constraints (tasks.md lines 62-118) assigns sole-editor status per shared file: T-009 alone edits `guard-invariants.json`/`generate-guard-invariants.py`/the four generated files; T-007 alone authors `apply-human-copy.{sh,ps1}`; T-011 alone edits `PLUGIN-CONTRACTS.md`; T-012 alone stages `ship/SKILL.md`/`lite-spec/SKILL.md`. Every task's `tests/run-all.sh`/`.ps1` and staged `.github/workflows/test.yml` edit is an append-only, single-suite addition in a numeric order enforced via Blockers (verified transitively: T-002→T-001, T-003→T-002, T-004→T-003, T-005→{T-002,T-004}, T-006→{T-003,T-004,T-005}, T-007→T-006, T-008→T-007, T-009→{...,T-008}, T-010→T-009, T-011→{...,T-010}, T-012→{T-009,T-011}), so no two tasks can land a competing edit out of order. `CHANGELOG.md` edits are append-only distinct entries per task, never editing another task's entry in place.

Every Blockers entry is explicitly justified in the task's own 'Depends On' prose as either a genuine functional dependency (e.g. T-003 on T-002 because 'the sidecar's HMAC preimage is canonical-JSON bytes'; T-006 on T-003/T-004/T-005 because it recomputes/re-derives their outputs) or is transparently labeled a non-functional, shared-file numeric-order serialization blocker only (e.g. T-002 on T-001, T-004 on T-003, T-007 on T-006: 'this task's own functional content ... has no ... dependency on' the blocking task's artifacts). Because each such serialization-only blocker is disclosed rather than presented as a hidden functional dependency, none misleads an implementer about genuine execution order. No missing functional blocker was found: e.g. T-012's dependency on T-008's handshake wiring is transitively covered via its declared Blockers on T-009 and T-011, both of which themselves depend on T-008.

SKIP: no bugfix or debugging task in scope. All 13 tasks (T-001..T-013) are net-new feature/security-infrastructure implementation or closing-audit tasks; none is scoped as a bugfix, regression fix, debugging, failure-diagnosis, flaky-test resolution, or incident-remediation task.
